title: A: The First Measure
meter: Prose (the Upaniṣad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pāda and mātrā, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
devanagari: ह वै सर्वान्कामानादिश्च भवति य एवं वेद॥
iast: ha vai sarvān kāmān ādiś ca bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
translation: Vaiśvānara, whose field is waking, is A, the first measure: because A pervades (āpti) all speech, or because it comes first (ādi). Whoever knows this obtains all desires and becomes first.
translation_hi: जाग्रत अवस्था वाला वैश्वानर अकार है, पहली मात्रा, क्योंकि अकार सब में व्याप्त है (आप्ति) या क्योंकि वह आदि में है। जो ऐसा जानता है वह सब कामनाएँ प्राप्त करता है और प्रथम होता है।

words.note: veda = 'knows', from √vid, the root of the word Veda.

grammar: Wordplay (nirukta): A is linked to आप्ति and आदि, words that begin with ā.
A truly pervades: in Devanagari every consonant letter carries the vowel a inside it: क = k + a. And अ is the first letter of the alphabet.
Ablative of cause: आप्तेः, आदिमत्त्वात् 'because of…', like पवनवेगात् in the bamboo verse.
